question: When a system of linear equation is consistent and inconsistent? Give an example for each. Test the consistency and solve the system of equations: x - 2y = 5, -x + y + 5z = 2, y + z = 0
answer:
Solution:

Given

x – 2y = 5   …………..(i)

-x + y + 5z = 2 …………..(ii)

y + z = 0 ………………..(iii)

The given equations can be written in the form

Ax = b

Where

A = \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 0\\-1 & 1 & 5\\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}\), x = \(\begin{bmatrix}x\\ y\\ z\end{bmatrix}\), b = \(\begin{bmatrix}5\\ 2\\ 0\end{bmatrix}\)

Its augmented form is [A:b]

~ [A:b]

~ \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 0 & : & 5\\-1 & 1 & 5 & : & 2\\ 0 & 1 & 1 & : & 0\end{bmatrix}\)

R2 → R2 + R1

~ \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 0 & : & 5\\0 & -1 & 5 & : & 7\\ 0 & 1 & 1 & : & 0\end{bmatrix}\)

R2 → (-1) R2

~ \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 0 & : & 5\\0 & 1 & -5 & : & -7\\ 0 & 1 & 1 & : & 0\end{bmatrix}\)

R1 → R1 + 2R2 , R3 → R3 – R2

~ \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & -10 & : & -9\\0 & 1 & -5 & : & -7\\ 0 & 0 & 6 & : & 7\end{bmatrix}\)

\(R_3 \to \frac{1}{6} R_3\)

~ \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & -10 & : & -9\\0 & 1 & -5 & : & -7\\ 0 & 0 & 1 & : & \frac{7}{6}\end{bmatrix}\)

R1 → R1 + 10R3 ,  R2 → R2 + 5R3

~ \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 & : & \frac{8}{3}\\0 & 1 & 0 & : & \frac{-7}{6}\\ 0 & 0 & 1 & : & \frac{7}{6}\end{bmatrix}\)

From the above, We can say that

x = \(\begin{bmatrix}x\\ y\\ z\end{bmatrix}\) = \(\begin{bmatrix}\frac{8}{3}\\ \frac{-7}{6}\\ \frac{7}{6}\end{bmatrix}\)

This is the required solution.

question: What is the condition of a matrix to have an inverse? Find the inverse of the matrix \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 1 & 2\\ 1 & 0 & 3\\ 4 & -3 & 8 \end{bmatrix}\)  If it exists.
answer:
The condition of a matrix to have an inverse is If A is an invertible matrix then there is a matrix C such that

AC = I = CA

In such case, C is called inverse of A and write as C = A-1

Problem Part:

Given

A = \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & -1\\ -1 & 5 & 6\\ 5 & -4 & 5\end{bmatrix}\)

~ [A:I]

\(~\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & -1 & : & 1 & 0 & 0\\ -1 & 5 & 6 & : & 0 & 1 & 0\\ 5 & -4 & 5 & : & 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\)

Applying Reduced Echelon Form

R2 → R2 + R1,   R3 → R3 – 5R1

\(~\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & -1 & : & 1 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & 3 & 5 & : & 1 & 1 & 0\\ 0 & 6 & 10 & : & -5 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\)

\(R_2 \to \frac{1}{3} R_2\)

\(~\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & -1 & : & 1 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{3} & : & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{3} & 0\\ 0 & 6 & 10 & : & -5 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\)

R1 → R1 + 2R2 ,   R3 → R3 – 6R2

\(~\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & \frac{7}{3} & : & \frac{5}{3} & \frac{2}{3} & 0\\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{3} & : & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{3} & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & : & -7 & -2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\)

To have inverse, We should have one pivot element in each row but in above matrix R3 doesn’t have pivot element. So,  Inverse of Matrix doesn’t exists.

question: Find the least-square solution of Ax=b for \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -6\\ 1 & -2\\ 1 & 1\\ 1 & 7 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(b = \begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 2\\ 1\\ 6 \end{bmatrix}\)
answer:
Here,

A = \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & -6\\ 1 & -2\\ 1 & 1\\ 1 & 7\end{bmatrix}\) and b = \(\begin{bmatrix}-1\\ 2\\ 1\\ 6\end{bmatrix}\)

Now,

\(\hat{x} = (A^{T}A)^{-1} (A^{T}b)\)  ———– (1)

AT = \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 1 & 1\\ -6 & -2 & 1 & 7\end{bmatrix}\)

ATA = \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 1 & 1\\ -6 & -2 & 1 & 7\end{bmatrix}\)\(\begin{bmatrix}1 & -6\\ 1 & -2\\ 1 & 1\\ 1 & 7\end{bmatrix}\)

= \(\begin{bmatrix}1+1+1+1 & -6-2+1+7\\ -6-2+1+7 & 36+4+1+49\end{bmatrix}\)

= \(\begin{bmatrix}4 & 0\\ 0 & 90\end{bmatrix}\)

and

ATb = \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 1 & 1\\ -6 & -2 & 1 & 7\end{bmatrix}\)\(\begin{bmatrix}-1\\ 2\\ 1\\ 6\end{bmatrix}\)

= \(\begin{bmatrix}-1+2+1+6\\ 6-4+1+42\end{bmatrix}\)

= \(\begin{bmatrix}8\\ 45\end{bmatrix}\)

Since we have definition of least square; the set of least square solutions of Ax = b coincides with the non-empty set of solutions of ATAx = ATb

therefore

\(\hat{x} = (A^{T}A)^{-1} (A^{T}b)\)

Here,

|ATA| = \(\begin{bmatrix}4 & 0\\ 0 & 90\end{bmatrix}\) = 360 ≠ 0

then

(ATA)-1 = \(\frac{1}{360} \begin{bmatrix}90 & 0\\ 0 & 4\end{bmatrix}\)

then equation(1) becomes

\(\hat{x}\) = \(\frac{1}{360} \begin{bmatrix}90 & 0\\ 0 & 4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}8\\ 45\end{bmatrix}\)

= \(\frac{1}{360}\begin{bmatrix}720+0\\ 0+180\end{bmatrix}\)

= \(\begin{bmatrix}2\\ \frac{1}{2}\end{bmatrix}\)

question: Let T is a linear transformation. Find the standard matrix of T such that  T:R2 → R4 by T(e1) = (3, 1, 3, 1) and T(e2) = (-5, 2, 0, 0) where e1 = (1, 0) and e2 = (0, 1); T:R2 → R4 rotates point as the origin through \(\frac{3\pi}{4}\) radians counter clockwise. T:R2 → R4 Is a vertical shear transformation that maps e1 into e1-2e2 but leaves vector e2 unchanged.
answer:
We know,

Standard matrix (A) = [T(e1)   T(e2)  T(e3)   …………]

for this

A = [T(e1)   T(e2)]

By Question

T(e1) = (3, 1, 3, 1) = \(\begin{bmatrix}3\\ 1\\ 3\\ 1\end{bmatrix}\)

T(e2) = (-5, 2, 0, 0) = \(\begin{bmatrix}-5\\ 2\\ 0\\ 0\end{bmatrix}\)

\(\therefore A = \begin{bmatrix}3 & -5\\ 1 & 2\\ 3 & 0\\ 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\)

Question (b):

T:R2 → R4 rotates points about the origin through 3π/4 radians counter clockwise.

To find the standard matrix of T, we use the fact that rotating a vector in R2 through an angle θ counter clockwise is given by the matrix:

\(\begin{bmatrix} cos(θ) & -sin(θ)\\ sin(θ) & cos(θ) \end{bmatrix}\)

In this case, θ = 3π/4, so the matrix for rotating through this angle is:

= \(\begin{bmatrix} cos(\frac{3\pi}{4}) & -sin(\frac{3\pi}{4})\\ sin(\frac{3\pi}{4}) & cos(\frac{3\pi}{4}) \end{bmatrix}\)

= \(\begin{bmatrix}\frac{-1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{-1}{\sqrt{2}}\\\frac{-1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{bmatrix}\)

Answer (c):

T:R2 → R4 is a vertical shear transformation that maps e1 into e1-2e2 but leaves vector e2 unchanged.

To find the standard matrix of T, we note that a vertical shear transformation that maps e1 into e1-2e2 can be represented by the matrix:

\(\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2\\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\)

Since T leaves vector e2 unchanged, we can append a row of zeros to the bottom of the matrix to get a 4×2 matrix:

\(\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2\\ 0 & 1\\ 0 & 0\\ 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\)

So the standard matrix of T is:

T = \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2\\ 0 & 1\\ 0 & 0\\ 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\)

question: For what value of h will y be in span {v1 , v2, v3} if \(v_1 = \begin{bmatrix}1\\ -1\\ -2\end{bmatrix}\), \(v_2 = \begin{bmatrix}5\\ -4\\ -7\end{bmatrix}\), \(v_3 = \begin{bmatrix}-3\\ 1\\ 0\end{bmatrix}\) and \(y = \begin{bmatrix}-4\\ 3\\ h\end{bmatrix}\)
answer:
If y is in span {v1, v2, v3} then it can be written as

x1v1 + x2v2 + x3v3 = y

where x1, x2, x3 are scalar

The augmented matrix is

\(\begin{bmatrix}1 & 5 & -3 & : & -4\\ -1 & -4 & 1 & : & 3\\ -2 & -7 & 0 & : & h\end{bmatrix}\)

Reducing to Echelong form

Apply R2 → R2 + R1,   R3 → R3 + 2R1

\(~\begin{bmatrix}1 & 5 & -3 & : & -4\\ 0 & 1 & -2 & : & -1\\ 0 & 3 & -6 & : & h-8\end{bmatrix}\)

Apply R3 → R3 – 3R2

\(~\begin{bmatrix}1 & 5 & -3 & : & -4\\ 0 & 1 & -2 & : & -1\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & : & h-8 + 3\end{bmatrix}\)

\(~\begin{bmatrix}1 & 5 & -3 & : & -4\\ 0 & 1 & -2 & : & -1\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & : & h-5\end{bmatrix}\)

It will be consistent when h-5 = 0

Therefore, h =5

Hence, y be in span {v1. v2. v3} when h = 5

question: Let us define a linear transformation T:R2 → R2 by T(x) = \(\begin{bmatrix}0 & -1\\ 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x_1\\ x_2\end{bmatrix}\) = \(\begin{bmatrix}-x_2\\ x_1\end{bmatrix}\). Find the image under T of \(u = \begin{bmatrix}4\\ 1\end{bmatrix}\), \(v = \begin{bmatrix}2\\ 3\end{bmatrix}\) and u + v = \(\begin{bmatrix}6\\ 4\end{bmatrix}\)
answer:
Here, Given transformation T:R2→R2 defined by

T(X) = \(\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1\\ 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x1\\ x2\end{bmatrix}\)

A = \(\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1\\ 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\) is standard matrix of transforation.

Now,

T(U) = AU

= \(\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1\\ 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}4\\ 1\end{bmatrix}\)

=\(\begin{bmatrix}-1\\ 4\end{bmatrix}\)

Also, T(v) = Av

= \(\begin{bmatrix}0 & -1\\ 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2\\ 3\end{bmatrix}\)

=\(\begin{bmatrix}-3\\ 2\end{bmatrix}\)

Also

T(u+v) = A(u+v)

= \(\begin{bmatrix}0 & -1\\ 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}6\\ 4\end{bmatrix}\)

=\(\begin{bmatrix}-4\\ 6\end{bmatrix}\)

question: Let \(A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 5\\ -3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix}4 & -5\\ 3 & k\end{bmatrix}\). Determine the value (s) of k if any will make AB = BA.
answer:
Given

A = \(\begin{bmatrix}2 & 5\\ -3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\),   B = \(\begin{bmatrix}4 & -5\\ 3 & k\end{bmatrix}\)

By question,

AB = BA

\(\begin{bmatrix}2 & 5\\ -3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}5 & -5\\ 3 & k\end{bmatrix}\) = \(\begin{bmatrix}4 & -5\\ 3 & k\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2 & 5\\ -3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\)

\(\begin{bmatrix}8+5 & -10+5k\\ -12+3 & 15+k\end{bmatrix}\) = \(\begin{bmatrix}8+15 & 20-5\\ 6-3k & 15+k\end{bmatrix}\)

\(\begin{bmatrix}23 & 5k-10\\ -9 & 15+k\end{bmatrix}\) = \(\begin{bmatrix}23 & 15\\ 6-3k & 15+k\end{bmatrix}\)

Equating the corresponding element,

5k – 10 = 15

or, 5k = 25

∴ k = 5

6 – 3k = -9

or, 3k = 15

∴ k = 5

Hence, AB = BA when k = 5

question: Define determinant. Compute the determinant without expanding \(\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 8 & -9\\ -1 & 7 & 0\\ 1 & -4 & 2\end{bmatrix}\)
answer:
The determinant of a matrix is a scalar value that is a function of the entries of a square matrix. It is basically a special number that is calculated from a square matrix.

Given

\(\begin{vmatrix}-2 & 8 & -9\\ -1 & 7 & 0\\ 1 & -4 & 2\end{vmatrix}\)

Apply, R1 ↔ R3

\(~ \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -4 & 2\\ -1 & 7 & 0\\-2 & 8 & -9\end{vmatrix}\)

Apply R2 → R2 + R1,   R3 → R3 + 2R1

\(~ \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -4 & 2\\ 0 & 3 & 2\\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{vmatrix}\)

Determinant  = -(1 x 3 x -5) = 15

question: Define null space . Find the basis for the null space of the matrix \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\\ 2 & 3 % 4\end{bmatrix}\)
answer:
Let A be a m x n matrix. Then, the null space of A, denoted by nulA, is the set of all vectors x ∈ Rn, such that Ax = 0 i.e.

Nul A = {x ∈ Rn : Ax = 0}

Note: Nul A ≠ Φ

Given, A = \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\\ 2 & 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\)

Let the homogeneous equation be

Ax = 0, x = \(\begin{bmatrix}x1\\ x2\\ x3\end{bmatrix}\)

Now, the augmented matrix is

\(\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 & : & 0\\ 2 & 3 & 4 & : & 0\end{bmatrix}\)

Apply R2 → R2 – 2R1

\(~ \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 & : & 0\\ 0 & -1 & -5 & : & 0\end{bmatrix}\)

Here, x1 and x2 are basic variable and x3 is free variable

Now, Apply R2 → (-1) R2

\(~ \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 & : & 0\\ 0 & 1 & 5 & : & 0\end{bmatrix}\)

Apply R1 → R1 – 2R2

\(~ \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & -7 & : & 0\\ 0 & 1 & 5 & : & 0\end{bmatrix}\)

From 1st row,

x1 – 7×3 = 0

∴ x1 = 7×3

From 2nd row,

x2 + 5×3 = 0

∴ x2 = -5×3

The solution is

x = \(\begin{bmatrix}x1\\ x2\\ x3\end{bmatrix}\) = \(\begin{bmatrix}7×3\\ -5×3\\ x3\end{bmatrix}\) = x3 \(\begin{bmatrix}7\\ -5\\ 1\end{bmatrix}\)

∴ Basis for the null space = \(\left \{ \begin{bmatrix}7\\ -5\\ 1\end{bmatrix} \right \}\)

question: Let B = {b1, b2} and C = (c1, c2) be bases for a vector  V, and suppose b1 = -c1 + 4c2 and b2 = 5c1 - 3c2. Find the change of coordinate matrix for a vector space and find [x]c for x = 5b1 + 3b2.
answer:
Let’s find change of coordinate matrix from B to C.

\(P_{C ← B} = \begin{bmatrix}[b_1]_c & [b_2]_c\end{bmatrix}\)

Here, B = {b1, b2} and c={c2, c2} are bases for V.

Given,

b1 = -c1 + 4c2

b1 = \(\begin{bmatrix}c_1 & c_2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}-1\\ 4\end{bmatrix}\)

∴ [b1]c = \(\begin{bmatrix}-1\\ 4\end{bmatrix}\)

Also,

b2 = 5c1 – 3c2

b2 = \(\begin{bmatrix}c_1 & c_2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}5\\ -3\end{bmatrix}\)

∴ [b2]c = \(\begin{bmatrix}5\\ -3\end{bmatrix}\)

∴ change of cordinate matrix from B to C is

\(P_{C ← B} = \begin{bmatrix}[b_1]_c & [b_2]_c\end{bmatrix}\)

= \(\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 5\\ 4 & -3\end{bmatrix}\)

Also, Given

x = 5b1 + 3b2

x = \(\begin{bmatrix}b_1 & b_2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}5\\ 3\end{bmatrix}\)

∴ [x]B = \(\begin{bmatrix}5\\ 3\end{bmatrix}\)

Now,

[x]C = \(P_{C ← B} [x]_B\)

= \(\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 5\\ 4 & -3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}5\\ 3\end{bmatrix}\)

=\(\begin{bmatrix}-5 + 15\\ 20-9\end{bmatrix}\)

=\(\begin{bmatrix}10\\ 11\end{bmatrix}\)

[x]C = \(\begin{bmatrix}10\\ 11\end{bmatrix}\)

question: Find the eigen values of the matrix \(\begin{bmatrix}6 & 5\\ -8 & -6\end{bmatrix}\)
answer:

|A – λI| = 0

Now,

= \(\begin{bmatrix}6 & 5\\ -8 & -6\end{bmatrix}\) – \(\begin{bmatrix}λ & 0\\ 0 & λ\end{bmatrix}\)

= \(\begin{bmatrix}6-λ & 5\\ -8 & -6-λ\end{bmatrix}\)

Now,

|A – λI| = 0

\(\begin{bmatrix}6-λ & 5\\ -8 & -6-λ\end{bmatrix}\) = 0

(6-λ)(6-λ) + 40 = 0

– 36 – 6λ + 6λ + λ2 + 40 = 0

λ2 + 4 = 0

λ2 = -4

Hence, Given values are

λ2 = 4i2

λ2 =  (±2i)2

λ = 2i, -2i

question: Find the QR factorization of the matrix \(\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\ 3 & -1\end{bmatrix}\)
answer:

question: Define binary operation. Determine whether the binary operation * is associative or commutative or both where * is defined on Q by letting \(x * y = \frac{x+y}{3}\)
answer:
A binary operation * on a set A is a map A × A → A, written (a, b) → a * b. Examples include most of the arthematic operations on the real and complex numbers, such as addition (a+b), multiplication (a × b), subtraction (a – b) and so on.

Given binary operation * defined by x * y = \(\frac{x + y}{3}\) on Rational number (Q)

1) Check if * is commutative

x * y = \(\frac{x + y}{3}\)    ∀ x, y ∈ Q

y * x = \(\frac{y + x}{3}\)  = \(\frac{x + y}{3}\)

Since, x * y = y * x, So, it is commutative

2) Check if * is associative

∀ x, y, z ∈ Q

(x * y) * z = \(\left (\frac{x + y}{3}\right )\) * z = \(\frac{\frac{x + y}{3} + z}{3}\) = \(\frac{x + y + 3z}{9}\)

x * (y * z) = x * \(\left (\frac{y + z}{3}\right )\) = \(\frac{x + \frac{x + y}{3}}{3}\) = \(\frac{3x + y + z}{9}\)

Since, (x * y) * z ≠ x * (y * z), So it is not associative

question: Find the vector x determined by the coordinate vector \([x]_{β} = \begin{bmatrix}-4\\ 8\\ 7\end{bmatrix}\) where \( β = \left \{ \begin{bmatrix}-1\\ 2\\ 0\end{bmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix}3\\ -5\\ 2\end{bmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix}4\\ -7\\ 3\end{bmatrix} \right \}\)
answer:

[x]β = \(\begin{bmatrix}-4\\ 8\\ -7\end{bmatrix}\)

β = \(\left \{ \begin{bmatrix}-1\\ 2\\ 0\end{bmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix}3\\ -5\\ 2\end{bmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix}4\\ -7\\ 3\end{bmatrix} \right \}\)

Writing β in matrix form

β = \(\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 3 & 4\\ 2 & -5 & -7\\ 0 & 2 & 3\end{bmatrix}\)

Also, [x]β = \(\begin{bmatrix}-4\\ 8\\ -7\end{bmatrix}\)

We know,

x = β [x]β

= \(\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 3 & 4\\ 2 & -5 & -7\\ 0 & 2 & 3\end{bmatrix}\) \(\begin{bmatrix}-4\\ 8\\ -7\end{bmatrix}\)

= \(\begin{bmatrix}4 + 24 – 28\\ -8 – 40 + 49\\ 0 + 16 – 21\end{bmatrix}\)

=\(\begin{bmatrix}0\\ 1\\ -5\end{bmatrix}\)

Therefore, Vector x = \(\begin{bmatrix}0\\ 1\\ -5\end{bmatrix}\)
